content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To protect your store from shoplifters, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Draft a preliminary shoplifting policy (2 hours)
Step 2. Review policy with legal counsel (3 hours)
Step 3. Print employee conduct handbooks (1 day)
Step 4. Research high-resolution CCTV brands (4 hours)
Step 5. Designate a secure room for video monitoring (2 days)
Step 6. Establish a budget for security hardware (1 week)
Step 7. Purchase heavy-duty floor safes (5 hours)
Step 8. Interview private security firms (4 days)
Step 9. Conduct a final security drill (3 hours)
Step 10. Install motion sensors at all exits (6 hours)
Step 11. Conduct a store-wide risk assessment (1 day)
Step 12. Map out blind spots in the floor plan (3 hours)
Step 13. Test the alarm system responsiveness (1 hour)
Step 14. Hire a dedicated loss prevention manager (3 weeks)
Step 15. Consult with local police on crime trends (2 hours)
Step 16. Purchase and unbox camera equipment (4 hours)
Step 17. Mount cameras in high-traffic areas (8 hours)
Step 18. Apply for necessary security permits (2 weeks)
Step 19. Train staff on "verbal judo" techniques (4 hours)
Step 20. Install locking display cases for electronics (1 day)
Step 21. Create a "No Trespassing" logbook (30 minutes)
Step 22. Inspect the building's electrical capacity for new tech (2 hours)
Step 23. Set up a cloud-based video storage account (1 hour)
Step 24. Place "Under Surveillance" decals on windows (2 hours)
Step 25. Configure remote viewing on manager smartphones (2 hours)
Step 26. Sync sensors with the central hub (2 hours)
Step 27. Hire an IT contractor for network wiring (5 days)
Step 28. Conduct background checks on new hires (1 week)
Step 29. Install convex mirrors in corner aisles (4 hours)
Step 30. Organize a neighborhood watch meeting (3 hours)
Step 31. Purchase electronic article surveillance (EAS) tags (2 days)
Step 32. Order employee uniforms with name tags (1 week)
Step 33. Select a primary internet service provider (3 hours)
Step 34. Run ethernet cables through the ceiling (1 day)
Step 35. Develop an emergency communication protocol (5 hours)
Step 36. Distribute handbooks to all staff (2 hours)
Step 37. Buy a bulk supply of security ink tags (1 day)
Step 38. Perform a perimeter lighting check (1 hour)
Step 39. Schedule a follow-up inspection (2 hours)
Step 40. Install a dedicated security server (6 hours)
Step 41. Host a workshop on identifying suspicious behavior (3 hours)
Step 42. Calibrate camera focus and angles (4 hours)
Step 43. Update the employee emergency contact list (1 hour)
Step 44. Gather quotes from various security trainers (2 days)
Step 45. Define clear roles for floor supervisors (4 hours)
Step 46. Secure a business insurance policy rider (1 week)
Step 47. Assign unique access codes to employees (2 hours)
Step 48. Meet with a locksmith to rekey doors (3 hours)
Step 49. Install magnetic locks on stockroom doors (5 hours)
Step 50. Draft a "Code of Ethics" for security staff (4 hours)
Step 51. Test the panic buttons under the registers (30 minutes)
Step 52. Set up a "Suspicious Incident" digital folder (1 hour)
Step 53. Attach EAS pedestals at the front entrance (6 hours)
Step 54. Rearrange shelving to improve line-of-sight (6 hours)
Step 55. Install a "dummy" camera as a deterrent (2 hours)
Step 56. Survey the back alley for entry points (2 hours)
Step 57. Train the team on tag removal tools (2 hours)
Step 58. Test the silent alarm link to the police (1 hour)
Step 59. Inspect the integrity of the loading dock (3 hours)
Step 60. Finalize the contract with the security firm (2 days)
Step 61. Install a monitor behind the checkout counter (3 hours)
Step 62. Register the business with the local alarm board (1 day)
Step 63. Label all high-value inventory with trackers (1 day)
Step 64. Review the store's "Right to Search" policy (2 hours)
Step 65. Upgrade the exterior deadbolt locks (4 hours)
Step 66. Purchase a high-speed document shredder (1 hour)
Step 67. File the final security plan with the head office (2 hours)
Step 68. Paint yellow "Caution" lines near the exit (3 hours)
Step 69. Activate the 24/7 monitoring service (1 hour)
Step 70. Establish a "Banned Customer" database (4 hours)
